title: observability: enhance token-level & KV metrics, dashboard updates, and alert tuning
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We need better visibility into per-token cost and latency across the serving stack and improved KV-cache observability to diagnose regressions introduced by recent batching/quantization changes. This PR adds richer token-level metrics, KV-cache hit/miss timing histograms, and a set of Grafana dashboards and tuned alerting rules designed to reduce noisy alerts while surfacing real regressions.

Summary of changes: Adds a new token metrics collector that emits per-request and aggregated per-token histograms (latency, compute-tokens, billable-tokens), augments existing KV cache instrumentation with detailed hit/miss timing, and expands tags/labels to include model_variant, quantization_profile, and route. Introduces three dashboards (token-cost-latency.json, kv-cache-insights.json, token-tracing-overview.json) and a consolidated alert_rules.yaml that replaces several noisy thresholds with smarter anomaly detection windows and severity levels. Includes docs and tests.

Checklist:
- [x] Token-level histogram and counters (collector + exporter)
- [x] KV cache timing metrics and hit/miss counters
- [x] Dashboards for token cost/latency and KV cache insights
- [x] Alert tuning: reduce noise, add P1/P2 severities, anomaly windows
- [x] Backwards-compatible metrics names (kept existing names as gauges/counters)
- [x] Unit + integration tests for metric emission
- [x] Migration plan in docs for on-call

Testing and validation: Unit tests cover the collector and exporter logic; integration tests run a small canary workload and assert expected metrics appear in the metrics backend (tagged with model_variant and route). Staging deployment used synthetic workloads with and without caching to validate KV hit/miss histograms and to calibrate alert thresholds. CI: running build/test/lint, flake8, and prometheus-metrics smoke tests. Initial CI run had two flaky test failures (metrics export timing), fixed by increasing tolerances and debouncing exporter flush in a follow-up commit.

Rollout plan: Gradual rollout behind feature flag obs.token_kv_enhanced: begin with 10% of traffic for 48h, monitor dashboards and alert noise, then 50% for 24h, then full rollout. Alert rules default to dry-run in the first rollout window. On-call playbook updated in docs/observability/token_metrics.md.

Backward compatibility and migration: Existing metrics names are preserved; new high-cardinality tags are optional. Alert tuning is additive and will be enabled for relevant services by default only after the canary windows. No breaking API or customer-facing changes.

Add KV cache timing instrumentation and hit/miss counters
Alert rules: consolidate and tune thresholds with anomaly windows
Tests: unit and integration tests for metrics emission
Docs: on-call playbook and rollout instructions
Fix: debounce exporter flush to reduce flaky timing tests

Author (Aisha): Addressed by adding a rollup metric token_latency.p50/p95/p99 with model_variant and a sampled token_latency.sampled tag. Lowered P2 to match staging baselines; left P1 as-is. See commit 4 for changes.
Li Wei: Please add unit tests for exporter debouncing and ensure prometheus labels are stable when tags are missing.
Author (Aisha): Added tests and updated exporter to emit stable empty_string label when optional tags are absent. Tests added in test_token_metrics.py.
Sofia Ramirez: Approved — dashboards look clean and alert noise reduced in staging. Recommend merging after CI green and canary flag added.

release_notes: Enhances token-level and KV-cache observability: new token histograms and rollups, KV cache timing metrics, three dashboards (token cost/latency, KV cache insights, token tracing overview), and tuned alert rules that reduce noise while surfacing cost/latency regressions. No breaking changes.
